about: A wallet under the bus-stop bench

lines.text: On my way home yesterday, I noticed something brown lying under the bus-stop bench.
It was an old leather wallet, and it look as if someone had dropped
lines.note: Tense: the story is in the past, so it is 'looked'.

lines.text: it only minutes before. Inside were fifty dollars, a few card and a photograph
of two small children. There was also a identity card with an address in
lines.note: Article: 'identity' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an identity card'.

lines.text: my own estate. I decided to return the wallet myself instead of leaving it there.
The owner’s flat were on the ninth floor of a block near the market.
lines.note: Agreement: 'the owner’s flat' is one thing, so it is 'was'.

lines.text: An elderly man opened the door slow and stared at me without saying anything.
lines.note: Word form: 'opened' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'slowly'.

lines.text: When I held up the wallet, his face changed at once. He told me
that he had searched every shop he visited that morning. He thank me again
lines.note: Tense: the story is in the past, so it is 'thanked'.

lines.text: and again, and he tried to give I ten dollars as a reward.
I refused the money, but his wife insisted that I take two orange home.
They were the sweetest oranges I have ever eaten.
